feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant technical depth. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but impact would improve with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing scope from coordinator to director, which strengthens credibility and leadership narrative.  
- Strong blend of strategy, communications, web/CMS, analytics, and multimedia skills; this makes the profile versatile and well aligned to digital leadership roles.  
- Writing is polished and readable overall, with no obvious misspellings and only minor style issues.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable results beyond activity descriptions: e.g., email growth, engagement improvements, campaign performance, efficiency gains, budget size, or team size managed.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidating these would improve structure and make the CV feel sharper.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; choose one punctuation style for lists with/without Oxford commas; “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “French (basic working proficiency).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding leadership, modernization, and mission-driven impact will make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard phrasing.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter value proposition focused on digital strategy, platform modernization, and content operations.
- Add leadership and organizational scale cues already supported by the experience section, such as enterprise platforms, governance, or cross-functional coordination.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading cross-channel content, web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in platform modernization, digital governance, and workflow design that improves coordination, publishing efficiency, and audience engagement. Strong background in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap heavily with Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” is repeated in both the intro and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS and web operations • Editorial systems and governance • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Workflow and platform architecture • Stakeholder and cross-functional alignment • Advocacy and policy communications • Multimedia and live event production”
- Replace “Multi-channel communication” with “Cross-channel communications leadership” for stronger seniority and cleaner grammar.
- Change “Web & CMS administration” to “CMS and web operations” to sound more strategic and less purely administrative.
- Consider swapping in one more distinctive competency, such as “Platform modernization” or “Content operations,” to better reflect recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid mirroring exact phrases.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical breadth, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps with themes already covered in your NACo roles. Tighten it around highest-value outcomes, scope, and what is new at this more senior/consulting level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client value: “Serve as strategic communications consultant to a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal-based campaign experiences, and enterprise web improvement.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one sharper line: “Built cross-functional content workflows, governance standards, and analytics frameworks to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more outcome-led: “Designed and launched modular microsites, storytelling pages, and member toolkits in Drupal; provided front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Keep the AI search bullet, but add impact if possible: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content model, and discovery UX to improve findability.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “workflows,” and “analytics” repeat heavily from NACo; avoid using all three in separate bullets here.
- “Large public-facing web properties” is vague; add scale only if it differs from NACo.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It would be sharper if the opening were less list-like and if each bullet emphasized outcomes, team leadership, and transformation rather than channel ownership alone.

Suggested edit
- Replace the first sentence with a tighter scope-and-impact line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management, leading platform modernization and cross-channel strategy.”
- Tighten bullets around major wins: website migration, analytics stack expansion, in-house studio launch, and governance/operations improvements.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: budget size, team size, email engagement growth, social growth, video output, reporting efficiency, or publishing turnaround improvements.
- Example phrasing: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video work may duplicate earlier NACo bullets unless this version stresses building the studio and scaling in-house production capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what you owned at this level versus broader strategy/governance later.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter scope statement: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social, and video, supporting NACo’s advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add outcome-oriented phrasing where possible: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel” and, if available, add views, open rates, or production cadence.
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Built editorial planning and publishing workflows that improved coordination across communications, advocacy, and program teams and increased consistency of digital output.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthened editorial planning/coordination” and “improved publishing workflows” are repetitive; merge them.
- Avoid repeating team-building, studio/video foundation, or broad channel oversight already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctive strengths rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Content operations leadership” if you want stronger alignment with your recent consulting and director-level work.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixed constructions like “audience-focused.”
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable proof points for experience bullets, not this skills block.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicate Core Competencies almost exactly.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already reinforced in the header and multiple NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. Use this topline item to emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than repeating software names.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Lead with Drupal/CMS modernization since that aligns most clearly with the most recent consulting work and NACo site migration.
- Remove lower-priority or older platform names from this topline section unless central to target roles; keep niche tools in “Technical + IT.”
- Replace “jQuery” with “front-end implementation” unless the role specifically asks for legacy JS libraries.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, API integrations, Airtable” are already listed in “Technical + IT.”
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies and Technical + IT; avoid repeating it verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for recent leadership roles, but the item reads like a generic keyword list. It would be stronger if framed around decision-making, optimization, and executive reporting rather than just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Recast as capability-led, not tool-led: “Digital analytics & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace vague terms with outcome-oriented phrasing: swap “Leadership reporting” for “executive dashboards and decision-support reporting”
- Tighten and group related skills: “KPI framework design, user behavior analysis, SEO/performance monitoring, conversion and content optimization”
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: “analytics infrastructure for high-traffic Drupal environments”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating that exact phrasing.
- This overlaps with the NACo bullet on expanding analytics infrastructure, so keep this section tool/capability-focused rather than repeating the accomplishment.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with the broader “Multimedia & live event production” competency and several NACo bullets. Make it more specific to current senior-level capability and emphasize delivery scope rather than basic tools.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from task list to capability/outcome language: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ/multi-camera studio direction • Virtual event operations”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the in-house studio achievement.
- If accurate, add scale/context instead of tools alone, e.g. “Livestream and hybrid event production for advocacy programming, member events, and recurring executive content.”
- Keep only 4 concise phrases; “studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” can be merged into one stronger line.

- This partially duplicates “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies; keep this version more technical/execution-focused.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize primary platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize most relevant/current platforms first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If formatting allows, add proficiency/context rather than just names: “Drupal (enterprise CMS, migrations, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Keep this item platform-only; avoid adding CMS modernization or technical implementation terms here since those already appear elsewhere.
- If space is tight, consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it has meaningful recent use; it reads less central than Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus broader capabilities.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles; avoid repeating unsupported platform detail elsewhere unless tied to actual use.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools you’ve used recently and confidently.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Reorder by relevance/recency: JavaScript • HTML/CSS • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Consider dropping version numbers and older framing: use “HTML/CSS” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3”
- If accurate, sharpen with scope/level: “JavaScript/jQuery for front-end enhancements” or “API integrations and lightweight automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills; either remove them there or keep this section as the detailed version.
- If Cloudflare Workers and GitHub Actions were only lightly used, consider omitting them to avoid overstating depth.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, not just tools: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems.”
- Tighten and group by function: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: “for editorial planning, approvals, cross-team coordination, and process automation”
- Prioritize strongest/recently relevant platforms first; consider dropping weaker/older tools if not used recently.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and automation are already mentioned in Topline Skills; avoid repeating them unless this section is strictly a tools inventory.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar project-management tools; listing all four may feel padded unless each is materially relevant.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is clear but too bare compared with the rest of the CV. Since email is a major thread in recent roles, this item should signal level of use and strategic relevance, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (email campaign delivery, newsletter operations, audience engagement)”
- If accurate, add scope/context: “Used to manage recurring newsletters, campaign sends, and member/stakeholder engagement programs.”
- Keep naming consistent and concise; “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys” may read cleaner than using a slash.
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, place it first to reflect recency and strength.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating detailed email achievements here; those are already covered in NACo roles (“newsletters reaching tens of thousands”).
- Don’t add generic “digital communications” language that duplicates Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it read as the foundation-building role: team formation, early platform/process improvements, and hands-on production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence around 2–3 core contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and supervised a digital media associate’s day-to-day work.”
- If possible, swap “high-impact” for evidence-based language such as reach, frequency, engagement, or operational efficiency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or first establishing the format.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow language already used in later NACo entries unless you specify this role as the initial buildout stage.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize project coordination plus the “first podcast” achievement, and trim broad phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program teams; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific phrase like “produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, internal teams served, or audience/use case.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so the progression toward digital leadership remains clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia/video language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; position it as a coordination role with an early content innovation win.
